div.head: Quadr II Praef 13
div.ab: Unde librum istum, quem nostri temporis argumento constitui, solo principio, non fine conueni, uelut in orto delitiarum inter omnia uoluptatis odora pigmenta florem unum carpserim, siciensque Tantalus non fugientia, sed gratis acomoda fluenta laudauerim; successus uero bellicos et prolis sue gloriam musis doccioribus inuitaui, pro uoto suscipiens, si merum pacis riuulum nostro simposio propinaui.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 543 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: Hence this book, which I have composed on the matter of our time, I have put together only as a beginning, not as an end [?], as if in a garden of delights, among all the fragrant spices of pleasure, I had plucked one flower, and, a thirsty Tantalus, had praised streams not fleeing but freely at hand; but the successes in war and the glory of his offspring I have left as an invitation to more learned muses, taking it as the fulfilment of my wish if I have poured out a pure stream of peace at our banquet.
